properties.decision:
**DECIDED 2026-08-19 BY ANTHONY**, on a two-part question put to him with recommendations:

**(1) `Constraint` IS the right home for a closed value set with no schema file — and its framing gets fixed.** He took the recommended option over an honest refusal and over a split rule. **(2) The fix reaches ALL THREE SURFACES** that describe Constraint as numeric — the `capture-intent` routing table, the served `AGENTS.md`, and `add_constraint`'s own tool description — rather than skills-only or additive-only.

His reasoning is carried by the options he declined: an honest refusal would have been conceptually cleaner but leaves a fileless user with nothing actionable AND still requires fixing Constraint for the prohibition case anyway; the split rule ("Constraint for prohibitions, refusal for enums") asks the agent to draw a line subtle enough to erode.

⇒ DELIVERED the same day, `epoch:constraint-is-not-only-numeric`.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT RESHAPED THE QUESTION — **THE FORK DISSOLVED WHEN SOMETHING OUTSIDE THE DESIGN WAS CHECKED**

The node originally asked whether the vocabulary has a home for an enum. **It has two, both already in the schema, and the served surface instructed NEITHER.** The method is `dec:agent-navigates-content`'s own rationale: *"before choosing between branches of a fork, ask what already exists that would make the fork unnecessary. Design inward only after looking outward."* That decision records two prior forks dissolving this way; **this is the third.**

**HOME 1 — THE SCHEMA FILE, and it is the one that scales.** `SPECIFIES` is `Artifact → [Interface, Capability, Component]` with `format: openapi / protobuf / json_schema / graphql / asyncapi / idl` (schema/build.yaml:72-81). **An enum is defined IN a schema file.** Register the file, point the edge at what it defines; the agent reads it, the graph records where it is. No schema change, no new node type, and a project with fifty enums does not get fifty nodes.
  🛑 MEASURED: `SPECIFIES` appeared in exactly ONE served skill (`link-artifacts`, "on the interface it defines"). Its Capability and Component targets were documented **nowhere**, and `capture-intent` never mentioned it.
  🛑🛑 **AND `SPECIFIES` HAS NO TYPED TOOL.** Nine typed edge tools exist (`realizes`, `documents`, `satisfies`, `provides`, `consumes`, `constrains`, `allocate`, `decomposes`, `verifies`); SPECIFIES is not among them, so `create_edge` is the only way to draw it. **`skill_lint` caught this during the fix** — the new row named a `specifies` tool that does not exist and the build went red. That is the "three legs" gap in the open: instruction now present, tool still absent.

**HOME 2 — `Constraint`, for a value rule stated as intent with no file yet.** Requires ONLY `name` and `statement` (schema/core.yaml:77-99); `quantity`/`limit`/`direction` all default null. Its own hint reads *"A limit or rule the design MUST respect… 'no PII leaves the device'"* — the same sentence shape as *"status is one of draft, submitted, paid."*
  🛑 **A KNOWN, MEASURED, UNFIXED DEFECT UNTIL NOW.** `fact:defect-the-constraint-vocabulary-is-documented-as-numeric-so-the-right-node-is-ruled-out` (2026-08-15, `basis: measured`, graded HIGH by its own author): a genesis session modelling the US federal government read the prose, concluded *"numeric budgets only"*, and **left eleven constitutional prohibitions as Requirements that would report unsatisfied forever.** Its stated cost: *"it never produced an error — it produced a confident wrong conclusion."*

🛑🛑 **AND THE ROUTING TABLE BUILT FOR ALEX'S FIRST REPORT HAD INHERITED THAT EXACT DEFECT.** `capture-intent`:50 read **"a number with a unit"** as the only Constraint row. So the fix shipped in `c863a4b` (#180) to stop the agent handing modelling questions back to the user **carried the numeric-only framing measured as HIGH four days earlier**, with no row for a prohibition, a value set, or a schema file. Not wrong sentence-by-sentence — **narrower than the schema, in exactly the way that had already produced a confident wrong conclusion once.**

⭐ SO THE TWO DIAGNOSES COLLAPSED INTO ONE. The node asked "did the instruction fail, or is there no home?" **Neither. The homes existed and the instruction never named them** — so the agent, correctly finding no matching row, did the one thing the table's last row forbids and asked the user, rather than saying "no good home for this yet". Which was not even true.

📌 WHAT IS **NOT** SETTLED BY THIS, so it is not read as closing more than it does: `req:vocabulary-covers-information` (`deferred`) asks for something genuinely different and genuinely absent — entities two components exchange **in a form a computation can read**, so the graph can tell two interfaces carry the SAME entity and map one organisation's field to another's under a different name and unit. **That is the semantic-interoperability layer and NOTHING here delivers it.** A pointer an agent reads is not a type a detector can reason over. Kept apart deliberately.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE RECURRENCE, WHICH STANDS AND IS THE REASON THIS WAS INVESTIGATED

  · **2026-08-14** — Alex asked what node types to store his data models as.
  · **2026-08-14** — settled as `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user`; option (c), agent judgement, CLOSED as "observed failing".
  · **`c863a4b` (#180)** — *"Never ask the user which node type to use."* Merged.
  · **2026-08-18** — same user, asked how to model "enums". His reply: *"I don't know, you figure out how to model enums."* ANTHONY: *"he considers that reflow2 + agent's responsibility (and I agree), not his job to define how to model something."*

⭐ **THE FIX WAS PRESENT IN THE SERVED TEXT AND THE BEHAVIOUR RECURRED** — and the finding above says why, which is more useful than "agents drift": the instruction shipped **with a table that could not answer the question**. That is fixable without making the instruction louder.

🛑 STILL TRUE: a leaked question leaves no node, so `loop_status` read clean through both exchanges. Nothing in reflow2 can see this happen. `skill_lint` cannot check a table for COMPLETENESS — only that the tools it names exist.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD

(a) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — fix the table at the root: rows for a value set, a prohibition and a schema file, and correct the numeric framing on all three surfaces. Fixes Alex's case AND the measured US-government case in one act.
(b) **NOT SEPARATELY ADOPTED** — generalise the honest refusal into a rule. The table's last row already carries it and the new note strengthens it; not made its own mechanism.
(c) **NOT CHOSEN** — un-defer `req:vocabulary-covers-information`. It is not what Alex needed, it is large, and `dec:agent-navigates-content` argues for the thin answer wherever a pointer will do. **Explicitly still open as its own requirement.**
(d) **NOT CHOSEN, STILL LIVE** — make the leak observable so the agent files a node when it cannot route a modelling question. The only option addressing why this went unnoticed for four days and was found by a user.
(e) **CLOSED** — agent variance; already closed once as observed-failing, and this was its second observation.

⚠️ THE JUDGEMENT ANTHONY MADE, recorded because it was genuinely contestable: an enum is arguably a TYPE DEFINITION rather than a LIMIT, and reflow2's own design carried ~1 Constraint node, so there was almost no worked precedent either way. He ruled that Constraint takes it. **If that proves wrong in use, the fallback named at decision time was the honest refusal, not a new node type.**

⚠️ UNCHANGED TENSION: some vocabulary reaching the user is CORRECT, and *"is this value set fixed by a standard, or does it vary per deployment?"* is a real question only the user can answer. It is not the question that was asked here.
properties.name: DECIDED — a Constraint need not be numeric, and a data model lives in its schema file: both homes existed, neither was instructed, and the routing table had inherited a measured defect
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill from Alex's report 2026-08-18; investigated and settled 2026-08-19 on Anthony's instruction to take it on. The node was rewritten rather than merely answered because the investigation changed the question: "is there a home for an enum" turned out to be "there are two, and neither is instructed", which is a far cheaper problem than the one first recorded. The Constraint half is tied to fact:defect-the-constraint-vocabulary-is-documented-as-numeric rather than restated, because that defect was measured four days BEFORE the routing table shipped carrying the same framing — a future session must see that the table inherited a known defect rather than invented one, since that is the argument for checking served prose against the schema generally rather than fixing this one row. req:vocabulary-covers-information is held explicitly outside the ruling so the semantic-interop need is not read as closed. The missing SPECIFIES tool is recorded because skill_lint surfaced it during the fix and it is the "three legs" gap caught in the act.
